title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in - Verity Insurance
summary: Quarterly renewal and expansion check-in. Customer requests capacity upgrade for Q4 spike, additional EU region, and a one-year contract extension. Discussed dedicated vs hosted, VPC options, SOC 2/KMS requirements, pricing addendum and benchmarking plan.
transcript:
[14:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, good to see you all. I'm Lena from Redwood, with Diego our SE.
[14:05] Maya: Hi thanks, Maya here. We got the agenda — capacity, regions, and renewal, right?
[14:09] Diego: Yep, that's right. Quick note — we'll try to keep this to 45 minutes.
[14:12] Tom: Sounds good. We're on Pacific time, so morning for us.
[14:16] Lena: Great. Quick status check: your current Dedicated pool is at 60% average utilization across weekdays, but you mentioned a Q4 spike for claims processing, can you remind us of the expected delta?
[14:25] Maya: Yeah, so with the new auto-adjudication flow we're estimating about 2.5x peak token throughput during open enrollment, maybe 3x in worst case, so we need headroom. There is some uncertainty because model choice might change, but planning for 2x to 3x.
[14:38] Diego: Got it. Do you have particular latency SLOs for interactive workflows vs batch?
[14:43] Maya: For interactive agent we need sub-300ms 95th, for back-office batch it's fine to be a few seconds.
[14:50] Lena: Okay that's helpful. For 300ms 95th with the current model family we'll recommend increasing reserved vGPU capacity and enabling cross-region warm-standby in EU to handle geographic failover.
[14:58] Tom: On the EU ask — compliance wants EU data to stay in EU regions for certain clients. We need to add a dedicated capacity in eu-west-1; is that possible under our Dedicated contract?
[15:08] Diego: Yes, we can provision a dedicated pool in eu-west-1. It will be a separate reservation footprint, same features — autoscale, KV cache, and VPC peering if you want. There will be a regional pricing differential.
[15:18] Sara: Pricing differential — can you ballpark? Procurement needs something to present to finance.
[15:23] Lena: We'll send a pricing addendum. Ballpark right now: EU reserved capacity tends to be about 10-15% higher on committed rates versus the US region due to infra costs, but we'll confirm. We'll put exact numbers in the addendum.
[15:34] Maya: Okay thanks. Also security — we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and confirmation that keys can be managed via our KMS.
[15:41] Diego: Yes, Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated. For hosted there are some limitations but for Dedicated+Private you can bring your own key, HSM-backed. SOC 2 docs are in the shared drive, I'll re-share the link.
[15:50] Tom: Is VPC peering required for your KMS integration? We prefer not to open public endpoints.
[15:55] Diego: You can set up a private endpoint and use VPC peering or private link — both supported. We'll include the network diagram in the security packet.
[16:02] Maya: Great. On the contract extension — we are approaching renewal in Q3 and considering a one-year extension with capacity uplift. What's the process?
[16:10] Lena: Standard flow — we'll produce an amendment that shows your current committed units, proposed uplift options (10%, 25%, 50% increases), and the updated committed spend. For expansion we can do a blended rate for the new region and new capacity, and include a ramp credit depending on term length.
[16:23] Sara: Ramp credit — can you explain?
[16:25] Lena: Sure — for a one-year commit we typically offer a 2-4% ramp credit applied over the first quarter to offset initial utilization inefficiencies while you onboard additional workloads. Longer terms get higher credits.
[16:35] Sara: Procurement will want those numbers by EOD next Thursday if possible.
[16:38] Lena: We can do that. We'll aim to get the pricing addendum and contract amendment by 2026-07-02.
[16:43] Tom: Will you also include support SLAs? We have a medium-priority incident SLO of 2 hours and high-priority of 30 minutes.
[16:50] Diego: We can map your incident priorities to our Enterprise SLA. For Dedicated customers we already offer 1 hour on high priority as a standard, but we can commit to 30 minutes as an add-on. We'll include that as an option.
[16:59] Maya: Nice. Another technical ask — can we run an end-to-end benchmark with our in-house model (quantized 4-bit) to measure latency and token cost per inference?
[17:08] Diego: Absolutely. We can run a benchmarking session in a staging pool. Two notes: quantized models sometimes change memory access patterns so kernel selection differs; we should run a few sequence length distributions to be representative. Also, please provide a small prompt set and a snippet of the model binary or container image and we'll run the bench.
[17:23] Maya: I'll send the prompt set and the container registry link, but registry access might be restricted — can you pull from our private registry?
[17:30] Diego: Yes, we can pull with a temporary read-only token; we'll coordinate with Tom on network egress rules.
[17:36] Tom: I'll open a service account and provide read-only credentials, and we'll restrict IPs.
[17:41] Lena: Great. Competitors were mentioned earlier in your internal notes — just to confirm, are you evaluating Anthropic and Bedrock as alternatives?
[17:48] Maya: Yes, Anthropic for safety features and Bedrock because of the marketplace integrations. Cost-wise we're also looking at open self-hosted stacks. The tradeoff is us building infra vs Redwood managing it.
[17:59] Lena: Understood. We'll prepare a short TCO comparison and performance notes from our recent benchmarks.
[18:05] Sara: Are there any compliance flags with EU region dedicated pools? We need data residency assurances for certain clients.
[18:11] Diego: We'll set data-at-rest encryption with customer KMS and ensure ingress/egress stays in-region. Audit logs are exportable to your SIEM, and we can set retention windows per dataset.
[18:21] Maya: One more thing — can we add an opt-in for automatic canary rollouts for model updates? We want to avoid regressions in production.
[18:28] Diego: Yes, Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies. We can configure canary traffic percentage and auto-rollback on metric degradation. We'll include recommended thresholds.
[18:37] Lena: Ok to recap next steps — we'll share: 1) pricing addendum and contract amendment draft by 2026-07-02, 2) security packet and SOC2 link today, 3) schedule a benchmarking run (Diego to coordinate with Tom/Maya), 4) TCO comparison vs Anthropic/Bedrock by next week.
[18:53] Sara: That timeline works for procurement.
[18:56] Tom: We'll get registry access and the prompt set by end of day tomorrow.
[19:00] Maya: Thanks, appreciate you moving quickly.
[19:03] Lena: Thanks all. We'll follow up in email with links to docs and the pricing PDF. Bye.
[19:06] *call ends*
